deities: Lord Shiva (as a conical Jyotirlinga in his Sadashiva form - the 'hump' of Shiva's bull form per legend)
festivals: Maha Shivratri (observed at the winter seat, Omkareshwar Temple, Ukhimath)

history.dynasty: Legend attributes the original to the Pandavas; present structure traditionally linked to Adi Shankaracharya
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: the world-famous Kedarnath Temple is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas and one of the four Char Dham shrines, standing at ~3,584 m on the bank of the Mandakini river near the Chorabari glacier, below Kedarnath peak. Legend holds the Pandavas built the shrine to atone for the Kurukshetra war, and that Adi Shankaracharya renovated it in the 8th century. Built of massive interlocking grey stone slabs in Nagara style (no mortar), the temple withstood the devastating 2013 floods - the Bhim Shila rock behind it is credited with diverting the waters. The temple is open only ~6 months a year (April/May-November); in winter the deity's worship moves to Omkareshwar Temple, Ukhimath, and an akhand jyoti burns inside the locked shrine. In 2026 the doors opened 22 April at 8:00 AM (closing expected ~11 Nov, Bhai Dooj).

name: Kedarnath Temple
town_description: Kedarnath, in Rudraprayag district at ~3,584 m, is the most remote and the highest of the Char Dham shrines, set on the bank of the Mandakini river amid the Kedar massif. Accessible only by a ~16-19 km trek from Gaurikund (or helicopter), the town comes alive in the yatra season and is abandoned in winter when the temple closes.

travel.road: Road to Gaurikund (Sonprayag-Gaurikund shuttle), then ~16-19 km trek to Kedarnath; helicopter services from Phata/Guptkashi (per Mint)

visitor_information.best_time: May-June and September-October (temple open ~April/May-November; closed in winter)
visitor_information.opening_hours: HOURS VARY BY SOURCE (verify): Mint reports 4:00-7:00 AM aarti, 7:00 AM-3:00 PM general darshan, 5:00-7:00 PM evening darshan, closed 3:00-5:00 PM; another guide reports evening darshan till 9:00 PM
